title: What's New in Kotlin Jump
tagline: Three features that stopped at 4000 files
summary: Three features answer a question about an absence by walking the whole project, and each one stopped after 4000 files. On a project of 5088 sources their safety guards fired on every run, so they said nothing useful.

highlights.title: Manifest badges say something again
highlights.description: All 56 permissions measured across 51 manifests carried the same cautious label. With the full listing, 16 of them carry a real verdict.

highlights.title: The removal quick fixes come back
highlights.description: Remove unused resource, dependency and permission never appeared on a project above 4000 files. Their listing counts resource XML too, 6278 files there.

highlights.title: One ceiling for all three
highlights.description: The dependency badge, the manifest badges and the quick fixes behind them now share a single limit of 20000, and each keeps its guard for what lies past it.

sections.heading: Fixes
bullets: The manifest necessity badges read the project sources with a ceiling of 4000 files and fell back to a cautious label whenever it was reached.
The Remove unused quick fixes read a listing that includes resource XML, so they overran even sooner and offered nothing.
The dependency badge, fixed last release, could say 0 imports and grey a line that no quick fix would then remove.

sections.heading: Notes
bullets: Reading the extra files costs about a third more time, once per 20 second window, and only while a manifest or a Gradle file is open.
